summary: Intermittent websocket fragment interleaving after TLS session-ticket resume behind customer edge proxy
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent truncated or duplicated final JSON arrays on websocket streaming sessions. Impact: Several production flows (web chat + background mobile sync) are returning partial outputs (missing closing array bracket or duplicated terminal 'end' event) causing downstream JSON parsing errors in their backend and mobile apps. Environment: MercuryForms runs on a Private deployment (VPC) with an HA edge proxy (customer-managed) in front of Redwood's VPC egress; they use our iOS SDK in background URLSession mode for mobile sync and a Node websocket client on server-side. Problem first observed after their edge proxy upgrade (transparent TCP pooler) on 2026-03-04.

Observed behavior: - Websocket sessions are established and begin streaming. - On ~0.6% of sessions the final frames arrive fragmented or interleaved: server emits close/terminal event but trailing JSON array is split across fragments in non-sequential order, producing either a truncated JSON or a duplicated trailing element. - Issue happens only when connection reseat occurs while stream is active (their edge proxies reuse TLS session tickets and perform connection pooling). - Reproduction appears more likely for longer streams (>= 1200 tokens) and when client reconnection uses a reused session ticket.

Expected behavior: Streaming websocket sessions should preserve frame ordering and terminal-event atomicity across TLS session-ticket resumption and upstream connection pooling. Terminal JSON structures (final array/object) should never be split into interleaved fragments that lead to invalid payloads.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs long-running streaming request against hosted websocket completion on model gpt-open-8k-v1 in prod us-east-1.
2) From their edge proxy, trigger a connection reseat by forcing TCP connection churn (e.g., rotate backend pool, short connection TTL) while stream is mid-flight.
3) Observe final messages on client: occasionally see truncated JSON array or duplicated trailing object leading to parse failures.
4) More likely when using iOS SDK background URLSession reuse or node ws client reusing TLS session tickets.
Notes: We were able to reproduce in a synthetic harness when simulating a proxy that re-orders small fragmented application frames during connection rebind.
logs: Trace id: trace-20260305-73af | ws_conn_id: 7f3a9c | timeline: stream_start -> keepalive -> conn_rebind -> terminal_fragment_received (partial) -> parser_error
Server snippet: FRAME_SEQ: [1,2,5,3,4] detected for conn 7f3a9c before finalization (expected monotonic).
Customer-side stacktrace: SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input at parse (mobile-sync v2.3.1)
investigation_notes: 2026-03-05 09:20 PST - Initial triage by Support (Aisha): gathered client logs and reproduction steps; confirmed customer edge proxy upgrade correlates with start of errors.
2026-03-05 11:10 PST - Eng (Tomás) ran synthetic harness: simulated connection pooling + TLS session-ticket reuse; reproduced ~0.4% failure rate matching customer symptom set.

Hypothesis: edge proxy connection reuse + internal worker handoff combined with our websocket fragmentation logic can allow out-of-order assembly of small control and data frames when connection reseat happens during in-flight fragmented payloads.
Evidence: Server trace shows non-monotonic frame sequence numbers for affected sessions. Frame seq reordering occurs only when upstream connection id changes mid-stream (proxy rebind path).

Mitigations tried: 1) temporary customer-side workaround to disable aggressive TCP pooling at edge proxy - eliminated reproduction in their canary region. 2) toggling iOS SDK to avoid background URLSession reuse reduced mobile incidence significantly.

Next steps: Prepare runtime patch to make the websocket streaming reassembly tolerant to transient frame reordering at terminal boundary and ensure terminal-event atomic commit is idempotent. Add additional guard rails in edge-worker to buffer and reorder small terminal fragments by sequence id before handing to the parser.
comments: 2026-03-05 10:05 - Aisha Rahman (Support): Logged ticket with customer, requested tcpdump and SDK logs. Customer provided edge-proxy config and timestamped traces.
2026-03-05 11:30 - Tomás Ortega (Eng): Reproduced locally with harness. Assigned to streaming-runtime team for patching. Opening follow-up INT ticket for internal change (INT-4121).
2026-03-06 09:00 - Customer (MercuryForms SRE - Elena K): Confirmed disabling 'pool-keepalive' on proxy reduced errors in staging. Asking for ETA on permanent fix for production.

2026-03-07 14:20 - Tomás Ortega (Eng): Implemented candidate fix: buffer terminal fragments up to 200ms and reorder by sequence id before parse. Running canary on serving-runtime in our staging cluster.
2026-03-08 08:55 - Aisha Rahman (Support): Notified customer of canary testing and recommended temporary mitigations while patch is validated.
2026-03-08 16:40 - Customer (Elena K): Canary results look good in staging; will coordinate production rollout window with their infra team.
resolution: Workaround: Customer temporarily disabled aggressive connection pooling on their edge proxy and switched iOS clients to non-background URLSession reuse; both reduced error rate to ~0.01%. Permanent fix: deployed runtime patch that buffers and reorders terminal websocket fragments by sequence ID and makes terminal-event delivery idempotent. Patch rolled out to 10% canary on 2026-03-07, 50% on 2026-03-08, 100% scheduled pending customer production window. Post-deploy validation: customer reported no parse failures in staging over 48h after patch. Follow-up: add e2e test that simulates connection reseat and reordering; update streaming runbook to include proxy pooling guidance.
